'''Sterling''' "'''Scoot'''" '''Henderson''' (born February 3, 2004) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played for [[Carlton J. Kell High School]] in his hometown of [[Marietta, Georgia]], where he was a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]]. At age 17, Henderson signed with the [[NBA G League Ignite]] after graduating early from high school and became the youngest player in [[G League]] history. In his second season, he was selected as a [[captain (sports)|captain]] of the G League Next Up Game. Henderson was drafted with the 3rd pick in the [[2023 NBA draft]] by the Trail Blazers.

== Early life ==
Henderson was born in [[Marietta, Georgia]], to Chris and Crystal Henderson.<ref name="abrams">{{Cite news |last=Abrams |first=Jonathan |date=May 21, 2021 |title=Scoot Henderson Has Options. He's Choosing G League Ignite. |work=[[The New York Times]] |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/05/21/sports/basketball/scoot-henderson-g-league-ignite.html |url-status=live |access-date=May 21, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210521180018/https://www.nytimes.com/2021/05/21/sports/basketball/scoot-henderson-g-league-ignite.html |archive-date=May 21, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Scoot Henderson Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft Status and more |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/hendesc01.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230121171213/https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/hendesc01.html |archive-date=January 21, 2023 |access-date=January 19, 2023 |publisher=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref> His father is a coach and trainer, and his mother is a [[Health administration|healthcare administrator]]. His parents run the training facility Next Play 360° in Marietta, where they moved from [[Hempstead, New York]], shortly before Henderson's birth. He is the second youngest of seven siblings, including three sisters who played [[NCAA Division I]] basketball, and was nicknamed "Scoot" or "Scoota" because of how he would scoot across the floor as a baby.<ref name="beck">{{Cite magazine |last=Beck |first=Howard |date=November 18, 2021 |title=He Should Be in High School. And He's the Future. |url=https://www.si.com/nba/2021/11/18/scoot-henderson-g-league-ignite-daily-cover |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230121171217/https://www.si.com/nba/2021/11/18/scoot-henderson-g-league-ignite-daily-cover |archive-date=January 21, 2023 |access-date=January 19, 2023 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]}}</ref><ref name="gordon">{{Cite web |last=Gordon |first=Sam |date=October 3, 2022 |title=Hoop prodigy's journey takes detour to Las Vegas |url=https://www.reviewjournal.com/sports/basketball/hoop-prodigys-journey-takes-detour-to-las-vegas-2650991/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230121171217/https://www.reviewjournal.com/sports/basketball/hoop-prodigys-journey-takes-detour-to-las-vegas-2650991/ |archive-date=January 21, 2023 |access-date=January 20, 2023 |website=[[Las Vegas Review-Journal]]}}</ref>

== Professional career ==

=== Portland Trail Blazers (2023–present) ===
====2023–24 season====
The [[Portland Trail Blazers]] selected Henderson with the third overall pick in the [[2023 NBA draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Peterson |first=Anne |date=June 22, 2023 |title=Trail Blazers select Scoot Henderson with No. 3 in NBA Draft |url=https://www.nba.com/news/trailblazers-select-scoot-henderson-with-no-3-in-nba-draft |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230623021759/https://www.nba.com/news/trailblazers-select-scoot-henderson-with-no-3-in-nba-draft |archive-date=June 23, 2023 |access-date=June 22, 2023 |website=[[NBA.com]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref> He made his [[2023 NBA Summer League]] debut on July 7 against the [[2023–24 Houston Rockets season|Houston Rockets]] with 15 points, five rebounds and six assists. He left the game early due to a shoulder injury and sat out the rest of Summer League.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=McDaniel |first=Mike |date=July 7, 2023 |title=Scoot Henderson Leaves Sensational Summer League Debut Early With Shoulder Injury. He is now considered an NBA bust|url=https://www.si.com/nba/2023/07/08/scoot-henderson-shoulder-injury-leaves-sensational-summer-league-debut-early |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230709073528/https://www.si.com/nba/2023/07/08/scoot-henderson-shoulder-injury-leaves-sensational-summer-league-debut-early |archive-date=July 9, 2023 |access-date=October 9, 2023 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Fentress |first=Aaron |date=July 17, 2023 |title=Trail Blazers' Scoot Henderson out for remainder of summer league with shoulder injury |url=https://www.oregonlive.com/blazers/2023/07/trail-blazers-scoot-henderson-out-for-remainder-of-summer-league-with-shoulder-injury.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230721143507/https://www.oregonlive.com/blazers/2023/07/trail-blazers-scoot-henderson-out-for-remainder-of-summer-league-with-shoulder-injury.html |archive-date=July 21, 2023 |access-date=October 9, 2023 |website=[[OregonLive]]}}</ref> On October 10, Henderson made his preseason debut, putting up seven points, one rebound and six assists in a 106–66 victory over the [[New Zealand Breakers]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Holdahl |first=Casey |date=October 10, 2023 |title=Trail Blazers Shake Offseason Rust In Win Versus Breakers |url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-shake-offseason-rust-in-win-versus-breakers |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231011065235/https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-shake-offseason-rust-in-win-versus-breakers |archive-date=October 11, 2023 |access-date=October 10, 2023 |website=[[NBA.com]]}}</ref> Henderson debuted his first signature shoe during the Blazers' media day. He will be the seventh player in NBA history to wear a signature shoe in their debut game.<ref>{{Cite web |last=DePaula |first=Nick |date=October 2, 2023 |title=Nick DePaula: First Look: Blazers PG Scoot Henderson debuts his first signature shoe — the Puma Scoot Zeros |url=https://hoopshype.com/rumor/2357368/ |url-status=live Henderson made his NBA regular-season debut, putting up 11 points and four assists in a 123–111 loss to the [[2023–24 Los Angeles Clippers season|Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Deckard |first=Dave |date=October 25, 2023 |title=In-Depth Analysis of Trail Blazers-Clippers on Opening Night |url=https://www.blazersedge.com/2023/10/25/23932886/portland-trail-blazers-los-angeles-clippers-final-score-boxscore-stats-scoot-shaedon-sharpe-ayton |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231026063646/https://www.blazersedge.com/2023/10/25/23932886/portland-trail-blazers-los-angeles-clippers-final-score-boxscore-stats-scoot-shaedon-sharpe-ayton |archive-date=October 26, 2023 |access-date=October 25, 2023 |website=Blazers Edge |publisher=[[SB Nation]]}}</ref> On November 1, Henderson suffered a sprained right ankle and bone bruise against the ====2024–25 season====
During his second season, on January 14, 2025 Henderson put up a new career-high 39 points along with six assists in a 132–114 loss to the [[2024–25 Brooklyn Nets season|Brooklyn Nets]]. He made 66 appearances (10 starts) for Portland during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 12.7 points, 3.0 rebounds and 5.1 assists.

====2025–26 season====
On September 26, 2025, Henderson was ruled out for at least one-to-two months after suffering a left hamstring tear during a workout.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 26, 2025 |title=Blazers' Henderson tears hammy, out 1-2 months |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/46389369 |access-date=2025-12-13 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> On February 6, 2026, Henderson made his season debut, scoring 11 points, five rebounds and nine assists in a 135–115 victory over the [[2025–26 Memphis Grizzlies season|Memphis Grizzlies]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Trail Blazers' Scoot Henderson to make season debut Friday|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/47842404 |access-date=March 4, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

On April 22, 2026, Henderson scored a game-high 31 points in a game-two win against the [[2025–26 San Antonio Spurs season|San Antonio Spurs]] in the first round of the [[2026 NBA playoffs]], becoming the youngest Trail Blazer to score at least 30 points in a playoff game.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Trail Blazers Complete The Comeback To Take Game 2, Even Series Versus Spurs 1-1 |url=https://blazers.com/news/trail-blazers-complete-a-comeback-again-to-take-game-2-even-series-versus-spurs-1-1 |access-date=2026-04-22 |website=blazers.com |language=en}}</ref>

== Off the court ==
On June 15, 2022, Henderson signed a multi-year endorsement deal with [[Puma (brand)|Puma]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 15, 2022 |title=Welcome to the Fam, Scoot Henderson |url=https://www.puma-catchup.com/young-basketball-talent-scoot-henderson-joins-the-puma-family/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230121171214/https://www.puma-catchup.com/young-basketball-talent-scoot-henderson-joins-the-puma-family/ |archive-date=January 21, 2023 |access-date=January 19, 2023 |publisher=[[Puma (brand)|Puma]]}}</ref> In 2022, Henderson applied for [[trademark]]s on his name and his motto, "Overly Determined to Dominate." In the same year, he launched his own boys' and girls' [[Amateur Athletic Union]] programs.<ref name="TheAthleticJan2023"/> Henderson starred in ''[[Shooting Stars (2023 film)|Shooting Stars]]'' (2023), where he portrayed [[Romeo Travis]].<ref name="ShootingStars">{{Cite web |last=Radish |first=Christina |date=June 7, 2023 |title=AJ Wills Jr., Khalil Everage & Scoot Henderson on 'Shooting Stars' and Playing Basketball's Fab Five his shoe deal with puma was ended and he had to repay them $1.7 million and they're now taking him to  claims court to get their money|url=https://collider.com/shooting-stars-avery-wills-jr-khalil-everage-scoot-henderson-interview/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230607164257/https://collider.com/shooting-stars-avery-wills-jr-khalil-everage-scoot-henderson-interview/ |archive-date=June 7, 2023 |access-date=October 13, 2023 |website=[[Collider (website)|Collider]]}}</ref>
